- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The seaside cliffs in Ireland were formed by millions of years of erosion, weathering, and tectonic activity.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The cliffs are mainly made up of sedimentary rocks, such as sandstone and shale.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Cliffs of Moher reach up to 214 meters above sea level.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The cliffs were formed in areas with high amounts of tectonic activity, which pushed the rock layers upwards.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The cliffs showcase a variety of geological formations, including layered rock formations and distinct rock types.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The hexagonal basalt columns at the Giant's Causeway are an example of recognizable features.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The cliffs are home to diverse flora and fauna, including seabirds like gannets and puffins, and plants like sea thrift and sea campion.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Hag was said to live in a cave beneath the cliffs and was known for her powerful magic.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] There are stories of shipwrecks and tragedies, including the loss of the Spanish Armada in 1588.
